text:
alex: Quick brain-dump: want a fallback design that fuses latency + quality signals (perplexity/regression checks) so we avoid blind fallbacks when model is slower but still high-quality. Thinking control-plane publishes policy + probe spec, edge agent does fast local decisions. Thoughts?

maria: Love it. Key Q: how do we measure "quality" cheaply at the edge? embeddings distance to golden outputs? light-weight classifier?

sam: We can run a tiny regexp/heuristic for obvious hallucinations but also send sampled queries to a golden probe pipeline that scores outputs asynchronously. Agent uses recent probe score + latency to decide.

rachel: Also add tenant-level exemptions. Premium customers shouldn't be auto-degraded unless manual override.

kevin: Proposal: a prioritized fallback sequence instead of binary canary->stable: e.g. canary-v3 -> canary-quantized -> stable-v2 -> small-backup. This gives gradual quality tradeoffs.

alex: Yes. Fallback sequence is important. Policy proto snippet: 

```
policy {
  name: "quality_fusion_auto_fallback"
  p95_latency_ms: 300
  quality_drop_pct: 8.0 // percent worse on golden set
  sequential_test_alpha: 0.05
  probe_sample_rate: 0.01
  probe_prompt_set: "golden-quick-20"
  fallback_sequence: ["canary-v3", "canary-v3-q8", "stable-v2", "small-compact-v1"]
  cooldown_ms: 60000
  max_concurrent_fallbacks: 50
  tenant_exempt: ["acme-corp", "bigbank"]
}
```

john: We should use a sequential hypothesis test (SPRT) to detect quality drift fast with controlled error rates. Agent keeps a rolling SPRT state per policy version.

maria: For telemetry: log decision_ts, policy_version, state (OK/SOFT_FAIL/HARD_FAIL/LOCKED), probe_score_mean, latency_p95, fallback_target, trigger_reason. Retain for 30d for replay.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: pushed probe harness build to staging :package:

sam: Agent state machine idea: OK -> SOFT_FAIL (degrade to next in sequence, continue probing) -> HARD_FAIL (move further down sequence + backoff) -> LOCKED (manual). Each transition emits an event and starts cooldown.

rachel: Sticky routing: bind by session_id or request_id hash for the lifespan of an interaction to avoid mid-response switches. Also respect token_budget quotas to avoid excessive cost.

alex: Edge decision rules (ranked): 1) if tenant_exempt => keep route; 2) if control-plane forced_override => obey; 3) else if p95_latency > p95_threshold and probe_score < quality_threshold => soft fail to next variant; 4) if repeated soft fails within window => hard fail.

kevin: Ops safety: add a global kill-switch to disable auto-fallback and a region-level circuit breaker that prevents >X concurrent fallbacks per region. Also backpressure propagation so downstream caches don't amplify traffic.

john: Observability: store sample pairs (input, canary_output, fallback_output) + embedding cosine and a quality delta metric for a small sample per minute. Expose in canary debug UI.

maria: For experiments, we should run mirrored traffic for a week: mirror canary + fallback to measure quality loss and latency benefit. Also synthetic golden probes every minute.

sam: Implementation checklist: 1) policy proto design + versioning, 2) SPRT lib + probe harness, 3) lightweight Go agent with cache + sticky map, 4) control-plane push/subscription + /force/lock API, 5) debug endpoints (/policy/last, /probe/status, /sample-pair).

rachel: Runbook items: steps to freeze fallbacks, how to escalate when fallback increases error rate, tenant pin/unpin commands, and rollback playbook. Keep it <1 page for oncall.

alex: One more: cost-aware decisioning. If fallback increases CPU cost by >X% but yields only tiny latency gain, prefer staying on canary. So policy should accept a cost_weight parameter.

kevin: Also consider gradual ramp on the fallback sequence (percentage-based) to prevent traffic stampedes: e.g. move 5% -> 20% -> 100% over N minutes when transitioning down.

john: Security note: ensure policy push is signed and agents verify version+signature to avoid rogue fallback flips. Audit all policy changes.

alex: Action items: alex will write the policy proto PR, sam will prototype SPRT + probe harness, kevin will sketch fallback-sequence logic, rachel will draft the operator-runbook. I'll open an RFC issue with perf targets and sample matrix.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: RFC issue created: https://github.com/redwood/research/issues/2020 :memo:

maria: Nice. Also add a small per-tenant telemetry quota so we don't drown SFX with sample pairs.

alex: Agreed. We'll cap sampled pairs per tenant and region. Thanks all.
